bib.title: OK-VQA: A Visual Question Answering Benchmark Requiring External Knowledge

question: Can a VQA benchmark be built whose questions cannot be answered from the image alone and need outside knowledge, and how do existing VQA models do on it?
hypothesis: State-of-the-art VQA models designed for image-question association will degrade sharply when answers need external knowledge, and retrieved unstructured knowledge will help.
contributions: (a) we introduce the OK-VQA dataset, which includes only questions that require external resources to answer
(b) we benchmark some state-of-the-art VQA models on our new dataset and show the performance of these models degrades drastically
(c) we propose a set of baselines that exploit unstructured knowledge

method.summary: MTurk workers wrote knowledge-requiring questions about COCO images; 5 other workers answered each; questions were manually filtered and answer-balanced, giving 14,055 questions. Benchmarked MLP, Q-only, MUTAN, BAN, a Wikipedia-retrieval model (ArticleNet) and MUTAN/BAN augmented with ArticleNet via a memory network, plus oracles and ablations.

datasets.name: OK-VQA
datasets.split: COCO original 80k-40k train and val splits used as train and test
datasets.source: random COCO images; questions and answers from Amazon MTurk; 5 answer annotations per question
datasets.preprocessing: Manual filter from 86,700 collected questions to 34,921; then removed questions if an answer was the most common answer more than 5 times (uniform answer distribution); removed questions with no inter-annotator agreement. Answers Porter-stemmed for scoring.

datasets.name: Wikipedia (snapshot via Chen et al. 2017 retrieval model)
datasets.size: about 100 articles retrieved per question; title plus T=5 sentences each
datasets.source: Wikipedia search API top article per query
datasets.preprocessing: queries = every single query word and every two-word combination of non-stop question words and top ImageNet, Places2 and COCO detector classes; sentences ranked by unique query words, then total query words, then article order

models.name: MUTAN (attention version)
models.architecture: multimodal Tucker fusion; ResNet-152 fc7 features; parameters of the single best model of Ben-younes et al.

models.name: BAN (single model)
models.architecture: bilinear attention network, Faster R-CNN features trained on COCO train

models.name: MLP
models.architecture: 3 hidden layers, ReLU, hidden size 2048, concatenates image and question features after skip-thought GRU and one FC layer each; ResNet-152 fc7

models.name: Q-Only
models.architecture: same as MLP, question features only

models.name: ArticleNet (AN)
models.architecture: GRUs over question, title, sentences with ResNet-152 image features; predicts answer in word, sentence, title, article

models.name: MUTAN+AN and BAN+AN
models.architecture: top N_art=20 ArticleNet sentence hidden states fed to an end-to-end memory network (2 hops, hidden 300); output concatenated into MUTAN after attention fusion / into BAN before final classifier

training.objective: VQA answer classification over top-2000 answers (not stated explicitly; inferred from answer vocabulary); ArticleNet: predict whether and where ground-truth answer appears in article, sentence, word (sigmoid outputs)
training.regularisation: batch normalization on FC layers of ArticleNet; balanced positive/negative articles

inference.decoding: classification over answer vocabulary; ArticleNet picks top word by a_wi * a_sent
inference.samples: single run per model reported; seeds not stated
inference.retrieval: Wikipedia search API, top article per query, about 100 articles per question, 5 sentences each; top 20 predicted sentences used by VQA models

metrics.name: VQA score (OK-VQA)
metrics.definition: common VQA metric of Antol et al. 2015, but each of the 5 answer annotations is used twice (10 in the original); answers Porter-stemmed

eval.protocol: single reported number per model on the 5,046-question test set; per-category breakdown by 10 MTurk-assigned knowledge categories plus Other; no significance test, no seeds

evidence.quote: but use each of our answer annotations twice, since we have 5 answer annotations

results.claim: MUTAN scores 26.41 and BAN 25.17 on the full OK-VQA test set, far below the best 2018 VQA v2 open-ended result.
results.setup: OK-VQA test, MUTAN with ResNet-152 features; baseline 72.41 is the 2018 VQA competition best real open-ended result on VQA v2, reported in text
results.table: Table 2, row MUTAN, column OK-VQA (26.41); BAN 25.17
results.note: 72.41 is quoted from the VQA 2018 competition, not measured here

results.claim: Adding ArticleNet knowledge improves MUTAN to 27.84 (+1.43) but BAN only changes from 25.17 to 25.61.
results.setup: OK-VQA test, MUTAN+AN with Wikipedia retrieval, N_art=20 sentences in a 2-hop memory network
results.table: Table 2, row MUTAN + AN, column OK-VQA (27.84); BAN + AN 25.61

results.claim: ArticleNet alone scores only 5.28 on OK-VQA.
results.setup: OK-VQA test, ArticleNet raw, can only answer from retrieved articles, not trained on VQA directly

results.claim: Oracle picking the better of MUTAN and ArticleNet per question reaches 28.47, showing retrieved knowledge is complementary.
results.setup: OK-VQA test, MUTAN/AN oracle takes best answer vs ground truth from raw ArticleNet or MUTAN; optimistic upper bound
results.table: Table 2, row MUTAN/AN oracle, column OK-VQA (28.47); BAN/AN oracle 27.59

results.claim: Question-only baseline scores 14.93, so images matter and the answer-bias filtering worked.
results.setup: OK-VQA test, Q-Only (MLP architecture, question features only); MLP with image gets 20.67
results.table: Table 2, row Q-Only, column OK-VQA (14.93); MLP 20.67

results.claim: Better visual features give only marginal gains: MUTAN with ResNet18, ResNet50, ResNet152 scores 23.64, 24.74, 26.41.
results.setup: OK-VQA test, MUTAN, visual feature backbone varied; Q-Only 14.93

results.claim: More than 78% of questions in VQA v1 can be answered by someone aged 10 or younger, so standard VQA needs little knowledge.
results.setup: MTurk age annotations on 10,000 VQA v1 questions (from Antol et al.); a rough proxy for knowledge needed
results.quote: The analysis shows that more than 78% of the questions can be answered by people who are 10 years old or younger.

results.claim: Filtering cut collected questions from 86,700 to 34,921 by manual knowledge filter, then to 14,055 after answer balancing and agreement filtering.
results.quote: Performing this filtering brought us down to 9,009
results.note: quote text spans a line with a ligature; see Section 3. Dataset size 14,055 also in Table 1.

results.claim: Plants and Animals (17%), Vehicles (16%) and Cooking and Food (15%) are the largest knowledge categories; Science and Technology is 2%.
results.setup: five MTurk workers labelled each question; plurality category, else Other (12%)
results.table: Figure 3 (text of figure), category Plants and Animals 17%

results.claim: ArticleNet helps most in brands, science and cooking categories; major portion of data needs knowledge outside Wikipedia.
results.setup: Table 2 category breakdown; authors' interpretation, not tested

results.claim: Training-set size ablation for MUTAN (5% to 100% of train) is plotted; authors use it to separate dataset size from question difficulty.
results.setup: MUTAN on random train subsets, evaluated on original test set; numbers only in Fig 7 (not in text)

limits: Small: 14,055 questions (5,046 test); authors say they trade size for knowledge and difficulty.
Answer-balancing (drop questions with an answer as most common more than 5 times) deliberately shapes the distribution and makes the set harder by design.
Authors concede the major portion of the dataset needs knowledge outside Wikipedia, such as commonsense or visual knowledge, so Wikipedia retrieval cannot cover it.
Single run per model; no seeds, variance or significance tests; BAN batch size, hardware and compute not given.
Only 2019 models (MUTAN, BAN, ResNet features) tested; scores of 25-28 are dated for modern pretrained VLMs; metric uses 5 annotators doubled, so not comparable to VQA v2 scores in the strict sense.
Whether each question truly needs outside knowledge rests on manual filtering and MTurk workers; no measured rate of leftover image-answerable questions.

terms.definition: VQA where the image content is not sufficient to answer the question, so methods must rely on external knowledge resources
frequency within a knowledge category divided by overall frequency, used to find category-specific words
